module_title: Modern Books - Jnanpith & Sahitya Akademi Award Winners
introduction: This intermediate level transitions to India's highest literary honors. TCS-pattern exams intensely test recent awardees (2024-2025), first-time winners, and historical milestones within the Jnanpith and Sahitya Akademi awards.

core_concepts.title: Recent Jnanpith Laureates (2024 & 2025)
core_concepts.description: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honor. The 59th Jnanpith Award (2024) was awarded to the celebrated Hindi author Vinod Kumar Shukla. The 60th Jnanpith Award (2025) went to the legendary Tamil poet and lyricist Vairamuthu.

core_concepts.title: Sahitya Akademi Award in English (2024 & 2025)
core_concepts.description: Navtej Sarna won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 in the English language category for his novel 'Crimson Spring'. In the previous year (2024), Easterine Kire won it for her novel 'Spirit Nights'.

core_concepts.title: Tomb of Sand (Ret Samadhi)
core_concepts.description: Written by Geetanjali Shree and translated by Daisy Rockwell, this novel won the International Booker Prize in 2022. It made history as the first book originally written in any Indian language (Hindi) to win this award.

core_concepts.title: The English Exception in Jnanpith
core_concepts.description: The Jnanpith Award was traditionally given only for the 22 languages in the 8th Schedule. In 2018, Amitav Ghosh became the first and only English-language writer to win this prestigious award.

important_entities.name: Amitav Ghosh
important_entities.key_fact: Books: The Shadow Lines, Sea of Poppies, The Ibis Trilogy.
important_entities.significance: The sole English-language recipient of the Jnanpith Award (2018).

important_entities.name: Vinod Kumar Shukla
important_entities.significance: A towering figure in modern Hindi literature, known for his unique, surrealist storytelling.

important_entities.name: Vairamuthu
important_entities.significance: Iconic Tamil poet and lyricist; the third Tamil writer in history to receive the Jnanpith.

important_entities.name: Navtej Sarna
important_entities.significance: Author of 'Crimson Spring', recognized for his outstanding contribution to Indian literature in English.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: For the International Booker Prize (like 'Tomb of Sand'), examiners love to ask for the name of the *translator*. Do not just memorize Geetanjali Shree; you must also know the translator, Daisy Rockwell.
If a question asks 'Who is the only author to win the Jnanpith for English?', the answer is Amitav Ghosh. This is an anomaly, making it a highly targeted trivia question.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Link the author strictly to their language and numerical edition for quick recall.
Navtej Sarna = Crimson Spring (2025 Sahitya Akademi English winner).

exam_strategy_tips: You do not need to memorize all 24 Sahitya Akademi winners every year. Focus exclusively on the winners in the **English** and **Hindi** categories, as these are the ones asked in national-level exams.
